questions.question: How does prompt caching reduce cost in the production RAG chatbot, and what cache hit rate is targeted?
options: It caches model weights in GPU memory to avoid loading them per request; target 90% hit rate
The system prompt plus reranked context are placed in a stable prefix that the model caches; token cost drops 3-5x on cache hits; target 60-80% hit rate
BM25 query results are cached in Redis; target 50% hit rate to reduce index load
The re-ranker scores are cached per query hash; target 70% hit rate
questions.explanation: Claude 4.5+ caches repeated prefixes at a 60-90% discount. By putting the static system prompt and reranked context first in a stable prefix, the pipeline achieves 60-80% cache hit rates and 3-5x cost reduction in steady state.

questions.question: What role do jurisdiction tags and role-based access labels play in the regulated-domain pipeline?
options: They determine which model (Claude vs Llama) handles each query based on data sensitivity
They are attached to chunks at ingest time and enforced as retrieval filters so GDPR content is never returned to a non-GDPR-role user
They trigger PII scrubbing on output for any chunk tagged as regulated
They select the appropriate reranker model based on the legal jurisdiction
questions.explanation: Chunks receive jurisdiction tags (GDPR, HIPAA) and role labels at ingest. The retrieval step filters by role+jurisdiction before running hybrid search, ensuring cross-jurisdiction or role-unauthorized content is never retrieved.

questions.question: What does RAGAS measure in the online evaluation of this RAG chatbot?
options: Token cost per query and prompt-cache hit rate
Faithfulness (answer grounded in retrieved context), answer relevance, and context precision per turn
False-positive rate of the Llama Guard 4 input classifier
p95 end-to-end latency from query submission to first response token
questions.explanation: RAGAS 0.2 runs online and automatically scores each turn on faithfulness (how well the answer is grounded in retrieved chunks), answer relevance, and context precision.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the golden set in this capstone's evaluation strategy?
options: A prompt injection suite used by the red-team to find jailbreaks
200 expert-labeled Q/A pairs with citations that serve as ground truth for measuring answer correctness and citation accuracy
A benchmark of 50 adversarial prompts testing PII extraction attempts
A weekly snapshot of the Arize Phoenix drift dashboard for SLO reporting
questions.explanation: The golden set is 200 Q/A pairs labeled by a domain expert with answers and citations. It is the ground truth used to score exact-citation match, answer correctness, and RAGAS faithfulness.

questions.question: What drift condition triggers an alert in the Arize Phoenix monitoring dashboard?
options: Any individual query's faithfulness score drops below 0.5
A 5% or greater weekly drop in retrieval quality metrics such as nDCG or citation faithfulness
Prompt-cache hit rate falls below 50% in any rolling 24-hour window
The re-ranker takes more than 500ms to score any single batch
questions.explanation: Arize Phoenix watches retrieval quality metrics weekly and alerts when nDCG or citation faithfulness drops more than 5%, which may signal that source documents have been updated without the index catching up.

questions.question: What layered guardrail approach does the production RAG chatbot use for safety?
options: A single Llama Guard 4 classifier on the final output only
Llama Guard 4 on input and output, NeMo Guardrails v0.12 for off-domain and policy rails, and Presidio to scrub PII from responses
A constitutional self-critique loop that rewrites any flagged response before returning it
An OPA policy gate that checks every retrieved chunk against a Rego deny rule
questions.explanation: Multiple layers: Llama Guard 4 classifies both input and output for policy violations, NeMo Guardrails enforce off-domain and topic-specific rails, and Presidio scrubs any accidental PII in the generated response.
